aiOverview.content: The Cuban Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR) are a heavily militarized,, Soviet-modeled force centered on a "war of the people" defensive doctrine, with an estimated 45,000–50,000 active personnel. While maintaining a small, aging conventional military, Cuba relies on a massive paramilitary network (over 1 million personnel). The military holds significant economic power, controlling roughly 4% of the economy. Key Aspects of the Cuban Military: Structure: Comprised of the Army, Air Force, and Navy, with the special forces unit known as "Avispas Negras" (Black Wasps). Personnel & Conscription: 2-year mandatory service for citizens aged 17–28. Equipment: Relies on older Soviet-era systems, including aging MiG-21, MiG-23, and limited MiG-29 fighters, alongside T-54/55 and T-62 tanks. Modernization & Training: Facing fuel shortages and economic constraints, the military has experienced training degradation, but recently engaged in joint training with Belarus for air defense systems. Paramilitary Bodies: Includes the Territorial Troops Militia (MTT), Youth Labor Army (EJT), and Border Troops (subordinate to the Interior Ministry). Role: Beyond defense, the military plays a key role in the economy through enterprises, notably in tourism and construction. Current Status: As of March 2026, the military is conducting exercises to prepare for potential external aggression. Key Figures: President: Miguel Díaz-Canel (Commander in Chief). Minister of the FAR: Corps Gen. Álvaro López Miera.
